correctness.rationale: For every prime p, Kummer borrowing shows max_k ν_p(C(N,k))=floor(log_p(N+1))−ν_p(N+1); an index p^r−1 attains the maximum. Odd N is handled by k↔N−k. At even N, all odd-prime maxima occur at even k; the even-index two-adic maximum equals the full-row two-adic maximum of row m by ν_2(C(2m,2j))=ν_2(C(m,j)). Odd-index two-adic maximum is attained by k=2^r−1. At an odd p, odd k=p^r−2 or modified digit k=p^r−1−p^j retains the full p-adic maximum except when N+2=2p^r; there the unique full-maximizer k=p^r−1 is even and the best odd k loses one p. This exhausts base-p digit patterns. Fresh independent exact LCM computation for N≤400 agrees, but the infinite theorem is proved by the borrow cases.

value.rationale: The all-N two-class restriction is a natural arithmetic refinement of the familiar Pascal-row LCM. It yields unexpectedly sharp complementary prime-loss laws, one purely 2-adic and the other triggered precisely by odd prime powers; neither quotient follows by routine substitution into the full-row identity.

final_claim: For all positive N, odd N has E_N=O_N=Λ_N; for even N=2m and w=m+1, Λ_N/E_N=2^{1+ν_2(w)−1_{w power of 2}} and Λ_N/O_N is the odd prime p if w=p^a for odd prime p, otherwise 1.
